new_statements.translation: 3.3 Tones. In the present state of our research on the language we posit the existence of three tones in Masmaje, namely high, marked by an acute accent (´), mid, which is not graphically marked here, and low (`), marked by a grave accent. Examples: tíwí 'fly', haawa 'wide', bàakò 'fear', káàkò 'snake', kidí 'earth', nùwáawí 'to be ripe', ʔúrdè 'granary', kaatù 'to leave', gùuri 'pillar'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Masmaje is described as a three-tone language (H, M, L, with M left unmarked); the sketch's phonology consists only of vowels, consonants and tones and makes no statement about word stress or accent d'intensité. Examples show lexical tone on every syllable (e.g. HH tíwí, LL bàakò, HL-falling káàkò, LHH nùwáawí), i.e. no positional 'accent' is described.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the author frames the three-tone analysis as a working hypothesis ('nous postulons') pending further research.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical (word-level) tone, illustrated on citation forms of nouns, adjectives and verbs (nine items). Tone-mark glyphs in the Google Books scanned snippet appear as an apostrophe for the acute and '?' for the glottal stop; they are normalized here to (´) and ʔ. The section title '3.3 Les tons' is confirmed by a phrase-exact query. The full page was not viewable (Brill paywall; Google Books page views 403), so the sentence is assembled from five overlapping verbatim snippets saved in the folder.
new_statements.identity_note: Alio 2004 describes 'le masmaje du Batha-Est' with a village list headed 'Liste des villages Masmadje' (Abdjidad, Allibeydad, Amkoofa, Amlammeena, Amzi'eef, Amriiri, Amchag..), Département du Batha-Est, chef-lieu Oum-Hadjer, 6,000 speakers (Beauvilain 1993) = Masmaje [mes], masm1239; he places it in the Mubi sub-group ('sous-groupe de la langue moubi', with Kajakse and Birgit possibly dialects of Mubi). The SIL 2007 survey (wordlist from Amlaména/Hilélé) reports the language as homogeneous ('La langue masmedje semble homogène'); no dialect subdivision is described by either source.
